lessons.title: Hello, panel
lessons.objective: Send one explicit text value to one explicit display sink.
lessons.prose: A panel is a bounded assembly of named nodes and cords. Run this one before changing it.
hints: The literal node produces text on its out port.
The stdout node consumes text on its in port.
lessons.solution: Connect greeting.out to output.in with the declared bounded cord.

accessibility.non_audio: The visible text output is the complete result.

lessons.title: Pull the cord
lessons.objective: Observe that a required input is not satisfied by a nearby node.
lessons.prose: Remove a cord on purpose. A useful diagnostic names the missing boundary instead of guessing a connection.
hints: The output node has one required input.
A node declaration does not create a connection.
lessons.solution: Restore the bounded cord from greeting.out to output.in.

accessibility.non_audio: The structured diagnostic is available as text.

lessons.title: Change the message
lessons.objective: Edit semantic configuration while preserving the same panel structure.
lessons.prose: Change the literal value, then select and move its faceplate. Source semantics and presentation are separate identities.
hints: Only the value configuration needs to change.
Moving a selected node does not rewrite source.
lessons.solution: Set greeting.value to the desired text and retain its explicit cord.

accessibility.non_audio: The output and source selection do not depend on color or sound.

lessons.title: Nothing up our sleeves
lessons.objective: Take the exact authored panel home and run it with the canonical command.
lessons.prose: Download preserves the real source you just ran. The same source is checked with conduct --check and executed with conduct --run outside the Tour.
hints: The command shown is the normal conduit command, not a Tour command.
lessons.solution: Download the source, then run conduct --check lesson.panel followed by conduct --run lesson.panel.

accessibility.non_audio: The executable result is represented by text output and canonical commands.

lessons.title: Direction matters
lessons.objective: See a wrong-direction cord rejected at the exact destination port.
lessons.prose: Ports are directional contracts. An output cannot stand in for an input, even when both nodes produce the same text type.
hints: Look at the port after the arrow.
A literal node only exposes an output port.
lessons.solution: Connect an output port to an input port, such as conduit/stdout.in.

accessibility.non_audio: The direction failure is exposed as a structured text diagnostic.

lessons.title: Fan-out is a choice
lessons.objective: Declare each consumer explicitly when one output feeds more than one sink.
lessons.prose: The literal output contract permits one or more connections. The two bounded cords are visible in source and each sink receives one value.
lessons.source:
panel 1

node greeting : conduit/literal {
    value = "Fan out.\n"
}
node first : conduit/stdout
node second : conduit/stdout

cord greeting.out -> first.in {
    capacity = 1
    max_value_bytes = 1024
    max_queued_bytes = 1024
    low_watermark = 0
    high_watermark = 1
    pressure = block
}
cord greeting.out -> second.in {
    capacity = 1
    max_value_bytes = 1024
    max_queued_bytes = 1024
    low_watermark = 0
    high_watermark = 1
    pressure = block
}
hints: The output node contract accepts more than one connection.
Each cord declares its own finite capacity and pressure rule.
lessons.solution: Keep two explicit cords from greeting.out, one to each sink input.

accessibility.non_audio: Both delivered values appear as text output.

lessons.title: Put a panel in a panel
lessons.objective: Use a composite boundary as an ordinary typed transform node.
lessons.prose: The composite exports only the ports it chooses. Its internal uppercase worker remains an implementation detail while the boundary remains substitutable for a primitive node.
lessons.source:
panel 1

composite example/uppercase {
    node worker : conduit/uppercase
    export input in = worker.in
    export output out = worker.out
}

node source : conduit/literal {
    value = "boundary"
}
node transform : example/uppercase
node sink : conduit/stdout

cord source.out -> transform.in {
    capacity = 1
    max_value_bytes = 1024
    max_queued_bytes = 1024
    low_watermark = 0
    high_watermark = 1
    pressure = block
}
cord transform.out -> sink.in {
    capacity = 1
    max_value_bytes = 1024
    max_queued_bytes = 1024
    low_watermark = 0
    high_watermark = 1
    pressure = block
}
hints: The composite has an input export and an output export.
The top-level cords connect to the composite boundary, not directly to worker.
lessons.solution: Keep the worker behind exported in/out ports, then connect the literal to transform and transform to the sink.

accessibility.non_audio: The uppercase transformation is visible as text output and source structure.
